description: Cloud Sync client behaviour, outside the wire contract (WIRE-CONTRACT-V4 §11.5, plans/U-01.md §4.1 as amended by plans/U-01b.md §4). Each scenario starts from `init` (when `legacyLocal` is not null, the client first imports it as its legacy `config.local` store) and runs its steps in order against a fake clock and a fake transport: `local` calls the SDK, `advance` moves the clock (firing debounce commits and the sign-out deadline), `network` goes online or offline, `respond` answers the one request in flight, `signIn`, `signOut` and `relaunch` act on the device, and `assert` compares the listed views. `requests` and `events` are what was sent and emitted since the previous assert. `settingCases` pins the setting routes a host derives from catalog entries (`syncedSettings`) and the user-block issues a publish reports. Literal data, not generated by an implementation.

rules.title: Every processed result removes its mutation; a request-level failure leaves the journal unchanged
A conflict is resolved as a new mutation on the server's version; the conflicting one is never resent
At most one unacknowledged revision mutation per record; later edits are held and rebased
A lost journal or client_mismatch gives a new clientId whose mutationIds restart at 1
Sign-out flushes up to 5 s, reports what stayed unsynced and keeps it in that subject's partition for 30 days
renamedTo and dropped are ok results; reads resolve old names through the pull's aliases
cursor_expired keeps the journal, takes a full snapshot and pushes the pending operations unchanged
The HLC's physical part is local time plus the last server offset
Edits stamped before the first server contact are re-stamped when the offset exceeds 5 minutes
Reads are the server snapshot plus pending operations
Writes are debounced per key, so a slider drag is one mutation
Journal and snapshot are partitioned by subject; nothing written as one subject is sent as another
Local-partition settings move into the subject's journal at sign-in; losers report origin merge
403 account_required leaves licence state untouched, keeps values local and offers sign-in
A relink that clears the binding or a merge alias is handled exactly like sign-out
A /sync 401 pauses Cloud Sync until the next document fetch and never touches licence state
A set on an enforced or hidden key is refused locally with managed_by_admin and journals nothing
An invalid stored value is kept, marked invalid and falls through to the next layer
A merge key sends one member op per changed member, never a whole set
A union record sends add and remove with observedSeq; a concurrent add survives
The journal survives a relaunch, debounced edits are committed on exit, and start pushes them
A key the catalog does not declare is an open setting: user scope, lastWrite, schema-less, at most 8 KiB of canonical JSON
A synced key is pushed with its route's scope; a local key stays on the device and never moves; a locked key is managed_by_admin; a secret, a flag or an invalid value is bad_request
The legacy config.local store is imported once at the HLC floor, so any newer cloud value wins
A lastWrite, max or min record is a stamped set the server resolves; on conflict the client takes the server copy and enqueues nothing
403 attestation_required blocks with reason attestation and any other 403 but account_required with reason forbidden; both keep the journal and wait for refresh
503 writes_paused on a push keeps the journal and shows paused, never blocked; the next trigger retries and a 200 push clears it

quota_exceeded and entitlement_required park a setting edit on the device, still read and never lost, until more room or a sign-in re-sends it as a new mutation with its clock; every other rejection reverts
A quota below the person's usage removes nothing, and a clear still passes

scenarios.name: optimistic-read-pending
scenarios.description: A pending set is read at once over the cloud snapshot, and the read moves to the cloud when it is acknowledged.

scenarios.name: max-policy-optimistic
scenarios.description: A pending set on a max key reads as the larger of the snapshot and the pending value.

scenarios.name: debounce-slider
scenarios.description: Three sets inside the debounce window become one mutation carrying the last value and the last edit's clock.

scenarios.name: clock-offset-folded
scenarios.description: A device clock 3 days fast stamps edits at local time plus the persisted server offset, and each response refreshes the offset.

scenarios.name: clock-slow-precontact-restamp
scenarios.description: Edits made 3 days slow before the first server contact are marked preContact, the first request is a pull, and they are re-stamped by the offset before the first push.

scenarios.name: clock-fast-precontact-restamp
scenarios.description: An edit made 3 days fast before first contact is re-stamped back by the offset, so it cannot win by a clock set ahead.

scenarios.name: lww-conflict-server-wins
scenarios.description: A stale lastWrite set comes back as conflict with the server copy; the client takes it, reports origin remote and enqueues nothing.

scenarios.name: conflict-then-ok-one-push
scenarios.description: A conflict followed by an ok in one push removes both; the next mutation's id is above both.

scenarios.name: request-failure-keeps-journal
scenarios.description: A 503 and a transport error leave the journal as it was; the next trigger resends the same mutationIds.

scenarios.name: conflict-rebase-new-mutation
scenarios.description: A revision conflict under a keep-local hook is resolved as a new mutation with a fresh id and the server's version as its base.

scenarios.name: one-outstanding-cas
scenarios.description: While a record's compare-and-swap is in flight, later edits of it are held and coalesced, then sent rebased on the result; another record's write is not held.

scenarios.name: account-switch-partition
scenarios.description: Alice's pending operation stays in her partition while Bob is signed in and is sent only at Alice's next sign-in.

scenarios.name: first-sign-in-empty-cloud
scenarios.description: Settings edited before any sign-in move into the subject's journal at sign-in (member ops for a merge key), wait for the first contact's pull, then upload.

scenarios.name: first-sign-in-newer-and-older-cloud
scenarios.description: At first sign-in a newer cloud value beats the moved local one (reported with origin merge) and an older one loses, with no prompt.

scenarios.name: sign-out-local-edit-sign-in-other
scenarios.description: After Alice signs out, a local edit lands in the local partition and moves to whoever signs in next, here Bob.

scenarios.name: account-required-on-push
scenarios.description: 403 account_required on a push is handled like sign-out: licence state untouched, the pending operation kept in the partition, values local, sign-in offered.

error.message: Sign in to use Cloud Sync.

scenarios.name: relink-clears-binding
scenarios.description: A relink that cleared the device's binding answers the start-up pull with account_required; values stay local and a document refresh does not lift it.

error.message: Sign in to use Cloud Sync.

scenarios.name: key-activated-device-local-only
scenarios.description: A device nobody has signed in on never calls Cloud Sync; its settings persist locally across a relaunch.

scenarios.name: merge-alias-subject-change
scenarios.description: A response naming another subject (a merge alias) is handled like sign-out; the old partition's pending operation expires 30 days later.

scenarios.name: unauthorized-pauses
scenarios.description: A /sync 401 blocks Cloud Sync with the journal intact and licence state untouched; only a document refresh resumes it.

scenarios.name: sign-out-flush-succeeds
scenarios.description: Sign-out commits the debounced edit, flushes it, and completes with nothing unsynced once the push is acknowledged.

scenarios.name: sign-out-flush-timeout
scenarios.description: A sign-out flush that gets no answer in 5 seconds completes with the operation unsynced and kept.

scenarios.name: sign-out-discard-unsynced
scenarios.description: signOut with discardUnsynced deletes the pending operations instead of keeping them.

scenarios.name: pending-expire-after-30-days
scenarios.description: A signed-out subject's pending operations, and its partition, expire 30 days after sign-out.

scenarios.name: on-sign-out-keep
scenarios.description: Under onSignOut keep, the snapshot and cursor survive sign-out, so the next sign-in pulls from the old cursor.

scenarios.name: journal-loss-new-client-id
scenarios.description: A relaunch with the journal lost generates a new clientId whose mutationIds restart at 1; the lost operation is gone.

scenarios.name: client-mismatch-regenerates
scenarios.description: 409 client_mismatch makes the client generate a new clientId, renumber its pending operations from 1 and resend.

scenarios.name: cursor-expired-with-pending
scenarios.description: cursor_expired keeps the journal, replaces the snapshot with a full pull, keeps the optimistic view and pushes the operation unchanged.

error.message: Cursor is older than the tombstone horizon.

scenarios.name: member-merge
scenarios.description: Setting a merge key sends one setMember or removeMember per changed member; a concurrent member edit from another device arrives with origin remote.

scenarios.name: union-add-remove
scenarios.description: A union record sends add, and remove with the cursor as observedSeq; an add the remover had not seen survives.

scenarios.name: renamed-and-dropped-keys
scenarios.description: An old build reads a renamed key through the pull's aliases, gets ok with renamedTo for a set on it, and ok with dropped for a dropped key (origin migration).

scenarios.name: locked-key-refused
scenarios.description: A set on a key the document enforces is refused with managed_by_admin and journals nothing, while the server's stored value stays out of the read.

scenarios.name: invalid-stored-value
scenarios.description: A stored value that fails the key's schema is kept, marked invalid and falls through to the next layer; a valid set replaces it.

scenarios.name: rejected-result-reverts
scenarios.description: A rejected mutation is removed, reported, and the read falls back to the snapshot (origin remote).

scenarios.name: relaunch-commits-and-pushes
scenarios.description: A debounced edit is committed on exit, survives the relaunch with its clock, and start pushes it.

scenarios.name: open-setting-synced
scenarios.description: A key the catalog does not declare is an open setting: read at once, pushed with scope user under lastWrite, read from the cloud once acknowledged, and another device's open setting arrives in a pull.

scenarios.name: open-setting-too-large
scenarios.description: A value over 8 KiB of canonical JSON is refused with bad_request and journals nothing; one of exactly 8 KiB is accepted.

scenarios.name: local-key-stays-local
scenarios.description: A local key set signed out and signed in is never moved at sign-in and never in a push, and always reads from the device, after sign-out too.

scenarios.name: secret-key-refused
scenarios.description: While Cloud Sync is on, a set or clear of a declared secret or flag, or a value its schema refuses, is bad_request; a key the catalog locks is managed_by_admin. None journals or sends anything.

scenarios.name: platform-scope-target
scenarios.description: A key routed with platform scope is pushed with scope platform; an open setting in the same push with scope user.

scenarios.name: config-local-import-loses-to-cloud
scenarios.description: The legacy config.local store is imported once at the HLC floor: a synced key and an open setting move at sign-in, and a newer cloud value beats the import (conflict, server copy, origin merge, nothing enqueued); a local key lands on the device and never moves; a locked or secret key is not imported.

scenarios.name: record-max-field-conflict
scenarios.description: A record in a max collection is a stamped set the server resolves on playtime; when the server keeps a larger one the push gets conflict, and the client takes the server copy and enqueues nothing.

scenarios.name: attestation-required-blocks
scenarios.description: 403 attestation_required blocks Cloud Sync with reason attestation: the journal is kept, licence state is untouched, later edits wait, and a document refresh resumes it.

error.message: This product needs an attested device.

scenarios.name: other-403-blocks
scenarios.description: Any other 403 blocks with reason forbidden and waits for a document refresh; unlike account_required it neither signs out nor offers sign-in.

error.message: Cloud Sync is not available here.

scenarios.name: writes-paused-keeps-journal
scenarios.description: 503 writes_paused on a push keeps the journal and the value and shows paused, never blocked, with no refresh needed; the next trigger retries, and the push that lands clears it.

scenarios.name: quota-rejected-keeps-value
scenarios.description: A set refused with quota_exceeded parks on the device: the value still reads, sync stays pending, the status gives reason quota, no rejected event fires and nothing is resent; it survives a relaunch, and a pull with no more room keeps it parked.

scenarios.name: quota-raised-retries
scenarios.description: Once a pull shows more room, a quota-parked edit is re-sent as a new mutation with its original clock, and lands.

scenarios.name: quota-lowered-deletes-nothing
scenarios.description: A pull whose quota is below the person's usage removes nothing on the device, and a clear still passes.

scenarios.name: terminal-rejection-reverts
scenarios.description: value_invalid is terminal: the value reverts to the snapshot and a rejected event fires. entitlement_required in the same push parks instead, and the next sign-in re-sends it as a new mutation with its clock.

settingCases.name: default-user-scope
settingCases.description: An Editable config key with no user block is a synced setting: user scope, lastWrite, listed, with its schema.

settingCases.name: platform-max
settingCases.description: A user block tunes the route: platform scope, the max policy on a number, and listed false.

settingCases.name: local-key
settingCases.description: user.sync local keeps the key on the device: a local route.

settingCases.name: catalog-locked
settingCases.description: managementDefault enforced or hidden locks the key whatever its user block says; the block is a no-op warning.

settingCases.name: secret-and-flag
settingCases.description: A secret and a flag are never a person's setting: refused routes (config.set answers bad_request while Cloud Sync is on).

settingCases.name: undeclared-key-is-open
settingCases.description: A key the catalog does not declare gets no route: the client syncs it as an open setting.

settingCases.name: array-merge-refused
settingCases.description: merge stays object-only: a list setting cannot combine (a set is an object of booleans), so a publish refuses it and no client derives routes.

settingCases.name: device-scope-retired
settingCases.description: user.sync device is retired with no alias: a publish refuses it (use local).
